srs.title: SRS Overview
srs.summary: Develop a UPI-based digital payments application for bank customers enabling P2P transfers, merchant scan-and-pay transactions, and integrated fraud monitoring. The system must enforce specific transaction limits, ensure real-time alerting for suspicious activity, guarantee scan-and-pay latency of <
assumptions: The bank has existing integration with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) switch for UPI settlements.
The bank possesses or can procure hardware security modules (HSM) compliant with PCI-P2PE standards for key management.
The bank's existing IT infrastructure supports microservices architecture for low-latency transaction processing.
Customer mobile devices meet minimum OS version requirements to support necessary encryption libraries.
stakeholders: Bank Customers (End Users): Utilize the app for sending/receiving money and payments.
Bank Customers (Merchant Users): Use the app to accept card payments via scanned QR codes (if applicable) or receive payouts.
Bank Operations/Compliance Team: Responsible for monitoring fraud alerts, managing transaction limits, and conducting periodic reviews.
Fraud Analysis Unit: Analyzes transaction logs and patterns to update fraud rules and prevent losses.
Third-Party Providers: Payment processors, card networks (for switching), SMS/Email gateways, and HSM vendors.
Regulatory Bodies: Adhering to RBI guidelines on fraud management, data privacy, and PCI-DSS compliance.

risks.text: Failure to enforce the 6-month log retention period (Answer Q4) could violate Evidence E2 (Section 70, implied context of logging and security controls).

risks.title: Latency Risk
risks.text: Meeting the < 3 seconds P2PE scan-and-pay latency requirement (Answer Q3) under high load while maintaining PCI-P2PE encryption rigor may pose technical challenges.

risks.title: Fraud Detection Risk
risks.text: Relying solely on the configured rules (Answer Q1/Q2) without dynamic behavioral analysis might miss sophisticated fraud scenarios mentioned in Evidence E4.

What is the precise maximum latency threshold definition (average vs. 95th percentile) for the < 3 seconds requirement?
Does the 6-month log retention apply globally or only to specific sensitive data types mentioned in Evidence E2 (Section 70)?

requirements.statement: The system shall enforce a per-transaction limit of ₹2,000 and a cumulative daily limit of ₹10,000 for all UPI-based transactions.
requirements.acceptance: The system must automatically reject any single transaction exceeding ₹2,000 or any daily cumulative total exceeding ₹10,000 across all user-initiated and merchant-paid UPI flows.

requirements.statement: The application shall block the digital payment product/service and notify the customer via email, SMS, and push notification immediately upon detecting the 5th consecutive failed login or invalid PIN
requirements.acceptance: The system must trigger an account lockout and send three distinct notifications (email, SMS, push) exactly after the 5th failed authentication attempt, adhering to the requirement

requirements.statement: The system shall transmit fraud alerts to the customer via SMS and Email with a latency of less than 3 seconds from the time of suspicious transaction detection.
requirements.acceptance: In a load test simulating 500 successful fraud detections, 99% of alerts must reach the customer via SMS or Email within 3 seconds.

requirements.statement: The system shall enforce the 6-month log retention period for all system, application, and user activity logs.
requirements.acceptance: The audit module must automatically purge all logs older than 6 months and flag any configuration set to retain logs for 7 months or less as non-compliant.

requirements.statement: The system shall support real-time fraud monitoring using rules based on transaction velocity, high-risk merchant categories (MCC), and new account activity.
requirements.acceptance: The system must generate real-time alerts when a transaction exceeds defined velocity thresholds (e.g., 3 transactions within 1 minute) or is initiated from a high-risk MCC.

requirements.statement: The system shall utilize PCI-P2PE certified solutions for all merchant Point-of-Sale (PoS) terminals and ensure Double Encryption of PINs for all card transactions.
requirements.acceptance: System configuration must validate that all connected PoS terminals are certified against the PCI-P2PE standard and support the Double Swipe functionality with no plaintext card/P2

requirements.statement: The system shall store no customer payment data (card numbers, CVV) in plain text; all data must be encrypted at rest and in transit using industry-standard algorithms.
requirements.acceptance: A forensic scan of the database must show 0 instances of plaintext card details or CVV numbers, and all API transmissions must utilize TLS 1.2 or higher.

requirements.statement: The system shall validate all incoming P2PE transaction responses and block processing if the latency for the cryptographic handshake or transaction authorization exceeds 3 seconds.
requirements.acceptance: End-to-end transaction time for scan-and-pay must not exceed 3 seconds under standard network conditions (100ms), measured over 5,000 test transactions.

requirements.statement: The system shall implement an automated breach detection mechanism that triggers within 24x7 hours of a suspicious transaction and initiates a fraud loss mitigation protocol.
requirements.acceptance: The monitoring engine must flag 100% of simulated suspicious transactions (based on configured rules) and trigger the incident response workflow within 24 hours of occurrence.

rejected.why: two processes to run; only pays off when requirements keep changing

too little rigour for high-risk or regulated systems
